key_insight: MM-Lifelong introduces hour-scale multimodal video data organized at Day/Week/Month densities and shows that current end-to-end multimodal LLMs fail on natural, unscripted long-range understanding. An agentic, memory-aware baseline improves robustness by explicitly handling temporal abstraction and retrieval.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between short, densely edited video datasets and real-world lifelong visual experience by providing a structured multimodal dataset and benchmarking long-range temporal reasoning and memory for models.
method: Curate MM-Lifelong: 181.1 hours of multimodal footage organized into Day, Week, and Month scales to capture varied temporal densities and natural, unscripted events.
Evaluate existing end-to-end MLLMs to identify failure modes in long-range comprehension and episodic memory consolidation on natural video streams.
Propose an agentic baseline that combines memory modules, retrieval, and policy-driven querying/summarization to better handle prolonged, sparse events.
impact: Provides a realistic benchmark and a practical agentic baseline that help researchers diagnose and mitigate long-term temporal failures in multimodal models, accelerating progress toward lifelong visual understanding.
